questions.prompt: Which of these random variables are **discrete**? Choose every one that applies.
options: The number of cracked welds found on a bridge girder
The time a technician takes to replace a bearing
The number of cars that arrive at a toll booth in one minute
The tensile strength of a steel coupon
The number of tests until the first chip fails
questions.explanation: Cracked welds, cars and tests are counted: 0, 1, 2, … They are discrete. A time and a strength are measured and can take any value in an interval, so they are continuous (Module 5).

questions.prompt: An inspector will check a batch of 10 valves. Let X be the number of valves that leak. Which statement is right?
options: X is a random variable; before the inspection its value can be any whole number from 0 to 10
X is a fixed number, the leak rate of the factory
X can be any number between 0 and 10, such as 2.5
X is the probability that a valve leaks
questions.explanation: X is decided by chance when the batch is inspected, so it is a random variable. It counts valves, so its values are the whole numbers 0, 1, …, 10. The probability that one valve leaks is a parameter of its distribution, not X itself.

questions.prompt: The number of trucks X waiting at a dock has this distribution: P(X = 0) = 0.10, P(X = 1) = 0.25, P(X = 2) = 0.35, P(X = 3) = 0.20, P(X = 4) = 0.10. What is the probability that **three or more** trucks are waiting? Give it to two decimals.
Two independent pumps are each working with probability 0.9. Let X be the number working. What is P(X = 1), the probability that exactly one pump is working? Give it to two decimals.
questions.explanation: Exactly one working can happen two ways: A up and B down, or A down and B up. Each has probability 0.9 × 0.1 = 0.09, so P(X = 1) = 2 × 0.09 = 0.18. Forgetting the second way gives 0.09.

questions.prompt: A CDF has F(2) = 0.70. What does that mean?
options: P(X ≤ 2) = 0.70: the chance that X is 2 or less is 70 %
70 % of the values of X are equal to 2
questions.explanation: The cumulative distribution function F(x) is P(X ≤ x), the sum of the PMF up to and including x. P(X > 2) is then 1 − 0.70 = 0.30.
